tasks.short: Assess natural contaminant removal from traceable evidence

steps.what: Retrieve site and contaminant data needed to assess natural removal from air, water or soil
Observe environments and take the planned samples or measurements of contaminants
Record contaminants measurements and environmental observations with site and sample references
Prepare comparable contaminant trends and fixed removal calculations for the environments assessment
Assess the evidence that environments naturally remove or reduce contaminants and write the limitations
Save the contaminants assessment finding and source references in the project file

tasks.design: Configure site-result views and sampling forms in {OPS_SYSTEM}, then reuse a checked calculation workbook in {SPREADSHEET}. The technician retains field measurements and the written evidence assessment in {DOCS}; calculations do not decide whether apparent attenuation is genuine removal.
tasks.previous_blocker: Result retrieval, repeated sample metadata and rebuilding trend tables fragment the assessment.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing site identifiers and approved calculation templates can reuse measured data.
tasks.still_hard: Distinguish removal from dilution, migration and sampling variation.
tasks.human_edge: Notice when the evidence does not support a natural-attenuation claim.

ambition.what: Compare contaminant trends against site conditions before recommending another monitoring round.

reach.learn: Detection limits, units and sampling comparability.

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: site-result filters, sampling forms and checked calculation templates can reduce clerical preparation while field work and environmental interpretation remain human.

assumptions: Boundary is the technician's assessment through a stored finding, not engineer approval of a remediation decision or regulatory submission. Actual field observation and writing are included; no additional progress log is added.

Existing laboratory staff provide sample id, analyte, value, unit, detection limit, date and method. Technician produces field measurements in s2 and captures actual findings in s3. Missing site/coordinate references and incompatible units are repaired within retained s1/s3/s4 time. OTHER is field measurement equipment.

Test native site forms and workbook templates first. S1 removes navigation, s3 repeated metadata entry and s4 repeated table/formula setup. Scientific interpretation and existing calculation runtime yield no saving. Ordinary author saves remain tiny, ungated and fully retained.
All shares are unmeasured focal labour estimates. Existing laboratory and engineer work is unchanged outside the denominator; incremental upkeep funds mappings and exceptional repairs.
unknowns: Result metadata compatibility and existing trend template coverage.
research_questions: Can measurements be compared without hiding changes in detection limits or sampling location?

already_counted.description: Field work, actual finding capture, comparability checks and assessment writing remain.

incremental.description: Maintain result mappings and calculation templates and repair incompatible records.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Central cuts 11 retrieval, 5.25 metadata and 9 table setup give 25.25 gross and 24 net. Cautious case: weak site metadata leaves s1 at 85%, unusual sampling leaves s3 at 90%, and incompatible methods leave s4 at 90%; gross 6 less upkeep 1.25 gives 4.75, above low 4.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Develop a resource-backed environmental work plan

steps.what: Define work plan scope, site constraints and required specifications with the engineering brief
Establish material, manpower and facilities needs from the selected work quantities
Develop the written work plan and specifications using the established resource needs

loop.purpose: Draft work-plan prose from the technician's explicit requirements and resource decisions
loop.input: Requirements, resource schedule and controlled template
loop.output: Draft with source-linked specifications and unresolved gaps
loop.check: Technician checks method, hazards, quantities and feasibility in s4; engineer reviews the final plan in s5
loop.stop: One draft; missing technical requirements stay gaps for manual resolution
loop.why_not_simpler: Site-specific sequencing and explanation require prose composition beyond filling quantities

steps.what: Check and revise the work plan specifications and material, manpower and facilities provisions
Approve the final work plan and specifications under the existing engineering authority
Release the approved work plan and specifications to the project workspace

tasks.design: Use checked resource tables in {SPREADSHEET} and the native plan template in {DOCS}, adding one bounded draft pass for the site-specific narrative. The technician validates the finished plan, the responsible engineer approves it under the existing process, and a separate action releases that exact version in {PROJECT}.
tasks.previous_blocker: Repeated resource calculations and first-version specifications slow preparation.
tasks.enabler_now: Templates and source-constrained drafts can reuse decided quantities and engineering requirements.
tasks.still_hard: Site hazards, safe sequencing and whether resources are genuinely adequate.
tasks.human_edge: Recognise a plan that is complete on paper but infeasible on site.

ambition.what: Present an explicit resource-needs schedule with each environmental work plan.

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: controlled plan templates and quantity tables can reduce repeated preparation while technical review and engineering authority remain human.

assumptions: Boundary covers the actual written plan and specifications through formal project release, not field execution or purchasing. Existing responsible-engineer review is unchanged, not newly invented labour.

Engineer supplies scope and technical constraints; technician captures requirements in s1. Existing quantity schedule and resource catalogue supply item, unit, quantity, crew category and facility requirements. S2 retains actual resource choices, missing-field capture and changed site assumptions.

Native templates and resource formulas are tested first. S2 removes repeated quantity arithmetic and table assembly, not resource judgement; s3 removes first-version prose only. S4 retains full technical checking and rewriting, with extra failed-draft recovery in upkeep.

S5 approves only the completed plan from s4; approval binds its exact version for s6 and changes void it. S6 is formal issue, not an ordinary working save; its tiny time is fully retained. Ordinary draft saves have no gates or saving.
Focal B91 excludes nine unchanged engineer shares. Shares are unmeasured task estimates. Incremental upkeep is deducted once.
unknowns: Existing engineering release process and reusable resource-table coverage.
research_questions: Which specifications can be drafted directly from current site requirements without new technical assumptions?

already_counted.description: Requirements, resource choices, draft correction, technical validation and release remain.
Existing responsible-engineer approval remains outside focal savings.

incremental.description: Maintain resource tables and template fields and recover failed drafts.

approvals.approved_version: final work plan and specifications version approved in s5; changes void release

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Central cut 10 resource preparation plus 10.5 writing over focal B91 gives 22.527 gross and 21.527 net. Cautious case: unusual resources leave s2 at 85% and novel specifications leave s3 at 95%; 4.5/91 gives 4.945 gross and 3.945 net, above low 3. Technical and engineer checks remain unchanged.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Improve chemical processes through controlled emissions trials

steps.what: Retrieve chemical process settings and toxic emissions measurements for the improvement study
Inspect chemical processes and diagnose likely causes of toxic emissions
Choose a chemical process improvement option and safe trial limits to reduce toxic emissions
Write the chemical process trial instructions, measurements and rollback conditions
Approve the final chemical process trial and exact permitted settings under existing change control
Apply the exact approved chemical process trial settings at the control interface
Monitor chemical processes and toxic emissions during the authorised trial and capture trial observations
Record and assess the chemical process trial results against toxic emissions and operating limits

tasks.design: Configure aligned historian and emissions views in {OPS_SYSTEM} and the trial-instruction template in {DOCS}. Keep diagnosis, option selection, controlled trial execution and assessment with people; the responsible engineer approves the final settings before the separate control action.
tasks.previous_blocker: Reconstructing comparable process evidence and copying standard trial fields distracts from diagnosis.
tasks.enabler_now: Native historian views and controlled trial forms can reuse known process tags and instructions.
tasks.still_hard: Reduce emissions without creating a different safety or quality problem.
tasks.human_edge: Notice adverse behaviour and stop within the approved trial conditions.

ambition.what: Compare proposed emissions improvements against matched operating periods before requesting a trial.

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: historian views and trial templates can reduce evidence preparation; chemical-process diagnosis, change authority and trial monitoring remain human.

assumptions: Boundary includes a supervised process improvement trial through its recorded assessment, not autonomous process control or permanent modification. Existing engineer change control is unchanged and outside focal labour.

Existing instruments produce time, process tag, setting, emissions value, unit and quality flag. Technician selects relevant periods and resolves missing tags in s1. Technician creates hypotheses and limits in s2/s3 and captures trial-specific instructions in s4. Native historian records measurements during s7; manual observations are entered and assessed in s8.

Test native historian joins and trial templates first. S1 removes repeated period alignment and screen navigation; s4 removes standard tag/instruction copying, not hazard reasoning. The technician retains all diagnosis, monitoring, observation capture and assessment. Existing instrument runtime creates no saving.

The completed trial instructions exist before s5; engineer approval binds exact settings, limits and rollback conditions for s6. Any edit invalidates it. S6 is an actual control change with fully retained small time, not an author save. No permanent change or automatic alert/send is introduced.
Focal B96 excludes four unchanged engineer shares. All times are unmeasured estimates. Missing joins and template failures are corrected in retained s1/s4 time with additional repair upkeep.
unknowns: Historian tag alignment and existing trial/change-control workflow.
research_questions: Can comparable operating periods be retrieved without hiding sensor-quality or load differences?

already_counted.description: Evidence interpretation, diagnosis, choices, trial writing, execution, monitoring and assessment remain.
Existing engineer change approval remains outside focal savings.

incremental.description: Maintain historian views and trial templates and repair failed joins.

approvals.approved_version: exact final trial settings, limits and rollback snapshot approved in s5; changes void approval

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Central cuts 9 evidence retrieval plus 4.5 trial fields over focal B96 give 14.062 gross and 13.062 net. Cautious case: irregular tag histories leave s1 at 85% and bespoke trial instructions leave s4 at 90%; gross 3.75/96 = 3.906 and net 2.906, above low 2. Trial and assessment work remain fully retained.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Select remediation technology from comparable site evidence

steps.what: Retrieve technologies and site evidence relevant to polluted air, water, soil or degraded ecosystems
Evaluate polluted site constraints and the practical suitability of candidate technologies
Prepare a comparable technologies table for clean-up and restoration requirements
Evaluate and select technologies to clean up polluted sites or restore degraded ecosystems
Write the technologies selection rationale, uncertainties and restoration constraints
Save the technologies selection record in the project file

tasks.design: Configure a source-linked technology catalogue view in {DOCS} and a comparison template in {SPREADSHEET}, using site evidence from {OPS_SYSTEM}. The technician retains site evaluation, technology choice and the actual written rationale; the tool neither ranks suitability by invented weights nor authorises implementation.
tasks.previous_blocker: Repeatedly finding technology limits and transcribing comparable attributes consumes evaluation time.
tasks.enabler_now: Native catalogue filters and checked comparison tables can reuse documented attributes.
tasks.still_hard: Transfer performance claims to a site's actual contaminant mix and ecosystem constraints.
tasks.human_edge: Reject a promising technology whose field assumptions do not hold.

ambition.what: Compare a shortlisted remediation option against its documented operating limits before a site trial.

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: source-linked technology catalogues and comparison templates can reduce retrieval and table transcription, while site feasibility and selection remain engineering judgement.

assumptions: Boundary includes site evaluation, the technician's delegated technology selection and its real rationale record. Final project spending and implementation authority are unchanged separate actions, not automated here.

Existing site and technology records supply contaminant, medium, concentration range, operating conditions, evidence source, version, cost basis and limitations. Technician assesses actual conditions in s2 and captures missing comparison attributes within retained s1/s3 time. OTHER is site inspection equipment.

Test native filters and comparison templates first. S1 removes navigation among known sources; s3 removes repeated attribute copying and unit display, not reading uncertain evidence or deciding relevance. No unsupported claim or scoring weight is generated.
Selection and rationale writing remain fully retained. The ordinary same-system save is tiny, ungated and carries no saving. No additional trailing implementation log is invented.
All shares are unmeasured focal labour estimates. Source-maintainer work is unchanged outside labour. Incremental allowance funds catalogue/comparison corrections.
unknowns: Catalogue metadata comparability and actual delegated selection authority.
research_questions: Which technology claims share a comparable medium, concentration and operating basis?

already_counted.description: Evidence interpretation, site inspection, comparison exceptions, selection and rationale remain.

incremental.description: Maintain catalogue references and comparison-field mappings.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Central cuts 10 retrieval and 11 table copying give 21 gross and 20 net. Cautious case: site-specific technology documents and incomparable claim units leave both s1 and s3 at 90% retained; gross 4 less upkeep 1 gives 3. Site judgement and selection remain unchanged.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: The technician retains field assessment and engineering judgement while reducing repeated evidence and plan preparation.
reach: Environmental data analyst: prepare traceable site trends.
Remediation engineer: prepare feasibility comparisons under existing supervision.
role.ambitious_version: Bring source-linked options and complete plans to the responsible engineer while preserving actual field work and change authority.
